title: Either way
summary: Prove a claim from p or q by showing that the claim follows in each of the two cases.

blocks.text:
The disjunction p ∨ q says that at least one of p and q holds. It does not tell us which. To use it, we must show that our conclusion follows from p and also follows from q.

By cases on a disjunction creates two goals. The first carries the left case, and the second carries the right case. The workbench keeps the second goal waiting while we finish the first.

To build a disjunction, choose the side you can prove. Left. changes the goal p ∨ q to p. Right. changes it to q. You do not need to prove both sides.

In the proof below, the p case needs Right. because p is on the right of the goal q ∨ p. The q case needs Left. Each case then closes from its own hypothesis.

challenge.prompt: Prove that p or q gives q or p. The assumption is given; handle both cases.
challenge.statement: Theorem or_swap. For all p q, p ∨ q → q ∨ p.
solution: By cases on h, as hp and hq.
hints: Split h into the p case and the q case.
Choose Right in the p case, then Left in the q case.

challenge.prompt: Write the disjunction with q on the left and p on the right. The kernel expects this order.
hints: Write q first and p second.

challenge.prompt: This attempt chooses the left side in both cases. Decide whether it checks.
challenge.statement: Theorem or_swap_attempt. For all p q, p ∨ q → q ∨ p.
steps: By cases on h, as hp and hq.
hints: In the first case, Left. changes q ∨ p to q.
The available hypothesis hp proves p.
